device.name: Android Device (Wireless Debugging / ADB over Wi-Fi)
device.notes:
Android 11 and later advertise their Wireless Debugging (wireless ADB) endpoint over mDNS/DNS-SD when the user enables it in Developer options. This project does NOT connect to the debug channel or do anything with it — there is no web UI and no control surface here. We DISCOVER the device, recognise it as an Android phone/tablet with wireless debugging enabled, and draw a phone pictogram. Nothing more.
DNS-SD service types (published by adbd, per AOSP adb_wifi.md):
  _adb-tls-connect._tcp — the TLS connect server, advertised while wireless
    debugging is active. The connect port is DYNAMIC and discovered here,
    not a fixed 5555.
  _adb-tls-pairing._tcp — the pairing server, advertised only during a
    pairing session.
  _adb._tcp — the legacy cleartext service started by `adb tcpip <port>`.
The service instance name is "adb-" + the device serial (ro.serialno) plus a random suffix added by the mDNS backend (e.g. adb-35121FDJH000R8-xyMD0H); a QR pairing instance is "studio-"-prefixed and a code pairing instance is guid-prefixed. adb mDNS records carry no meaningful TXT data.
There is no admin_url: wireless ADB is a debug transport, not a web console, so there is nothing to deep-link to. The serial is embedded in the instance name but carries a random suffix, so the stable key is the mDNS hostname and the display name is the advertised instance name.

enter_pairing_mode.indicator: The phone shows the pairing code and the pairing server's IP:port; _adb-tls-pairing._tcp is advertised while the dialog is open.
enter_pairing_mode.notes: The pairing server exists only while the pairing dialog (or QR scanner) is open, so the window is however long the user leaves it open; no fixed timeout is documented. The pairing-code instance is named adb-<guid> and the QR instance studio-<random>. The legacy `adb tcpip` route is different: it is authorised over USB by the "Allow USB debugging?" RSA-fingerprint prompt and then runs in cleartext with no pairing code.

procedures.basis: AOSP's adb_wifi.md (Pairing, pair and Pair with code sections) and the Android Developers adb documentation.
procedures.name: Pair device with pairing code

steps.action: Enable Developer options, then switch on Settings > System > Developer options > Wireless debugging and allow it on this network.
Tap 'Pair device with pairing code' and keep the dialog open.
steps.expect: A six-digit code and an IP:port are shown.

steps.action: Run the SPAKE2 pairing exchange against the advertised _adb-tls-pairing._tcp port with the code the user types in.
steps.expect: Pairing succeeds; the host then connects to _adb-tls-connect._tcp over TLS.

procedures.basis: AOSP's adb_wifi.md, Pair with QR code section (the scheme Android Studio uses).
procedures.name: Pair device with QR code

steps.action: Generate a 'studio-' service name and a password, and show them as an ADB Wi-Fi QR code.
On the phone, in Wireless debugging, tap 'Pair device with QR code' and scan the host's code.
steps.expect: The phone starts a pairing server under the requested studio- instance name.

steps.action: Find that instance over mDNS and pair with the password from the QR code.

exclusivity.recovery: Nothing to clear: the phone keeps a list of trusted hosts, and pairing another adds to it. If a paired host stops connecting, check that Wireless debugging is still on — the phone turns it off when it leaves the Wi-Fi network it was enabled on — and rediscover the connect port, which changes each time wireless debugging is switched on.

pairing.notes: Wireless debugging (Android 11+) is gated by a real pairing: the user opens a pairing session on the phone, a shared secret (the six-digit code, or the host's QR password) bootstraps trust over TLS, and the phone stores the host's RSA public key. From then on the host authenticates every TLS connection with its private key and needs no code, until the user forgets it. Entirely local — no account or cloud at any step. This project does not pair (identify-only); the block describes what any adb host must do. See `credentials.notes`.

pin.notes: The six-digit pairing code, shown on the phone in the "Pair device with pairing code" dialog alongside the IP:port of the pairing server, and typed into the host (`adb pair <ip>:<port>`). QR pairing reverses the direction: the HOST generates the service name and password and shows them as a QR code (WIFI:T:ADB;S:<name>;P:<pw>;;) that the phone scans. Either way the secret is fresh per session. What persists is the host's public key in the phone's trust store (/data/misc/adb/adb_keys), which every later TLS connect checks.

unpair.clears: One paired host's key (from the Wireless debugging paired-devices list), or every authorised host at once.
unpair.notes: Each paired host is listed on the Wireless debugging screen and can be forgotten individually. "Revoke USB debugging authorizations" in Developer options removes every authorised host key, USB and wireless alike. Turning Wireless debugging off stops the listener without removing any trust.

credentials.notes: Identify-only: no credential crosses to this app. ADB's own TLS pairing (the 6-digit code or QR) is between the phone and whatever debugging host the user chooses — not this app.

factory_reset.effect: Not applicable: there is nothing on this app's side to reset. Turning wireless debugging off (or revoking pairings) is done on the phone and simply withdraws the mDNS advertisement.

methods.description: No provisioning by this app. The user enables Wireless debugging on the Android device; discovery is the passive mDNS advertisement of _adb-tls-connect._tcp.

setup.notes: Nothing for this app to provision. Wireless debugging is enabled by the user on the phone (Developer options → Wireless debugging); once enabled, adbd advertises _adb-tls-connect._tcp and the device is discovered passively. This app neither pairs nor connects — it only recognises the advertisement.

rejoin.notes: Re-enabling wireless debugging re-advertises the service on whatever network the phone is on; identity keys on the mDNS hostname, not IP.

testing.notes: No hardware exercised by this project. The discovery signature is taken from the public AOSP adb source and its adb_wifi.md developer documentation, not from a capture of a specific phone. The service types are published by adbd itself and are Android-specific, so identification rests on the AOSP definition rather than any one device.

local_access.summary: The device is locally reachable over wireless ADB by any adb host on the LAN once paired — deliberately out of scope here; this project only identifies the device and does not open the debug channel.
